source_checks.passage: Standard Chartered's first-half pretax profit rose 9 per cent to US$4.78 billion (S$6.17 billion), beating analyst estimates and driven by strong wealth and global banking revenue.

However, the exact sentence used as the anchoring quote for claim-054 and claim-055 sits in the article's bullet summary block, which the publisher labels 'AI generated' four lines below it. source_checks.recommendation: Re-anchor claim-054 and claim-055 to the article body sentence (e.g. the 'US$4.52 billion average of 16 analyst estimates' line, which also supplies the consensus figure) rather than the block the publisher marks as AI generated.

claim_findings.passage: Lloyds' H1 2026 net income grew at a similar rate to peers' reported H1 2026 pre-tax profit
claim_findings.evidence: The round-1 conflation and the implied Lloyds consensus beat are both fixed -- the claim now names each metric explicitly and states outright that no Lloyds pre-event consensus figure exists in this run. What remains is the word 'similar': Lloyds' net income grew 9% (claim-002), Standard Chartered's pre-tax profit grew 9% (claim-054), but Barclays' pre-tax profit grew 17% (claim-053). One of the two peers is close to Lloyds' rate and the other is nearly double it, so 'a similar rate to peers' overstates the match.
claim_findings.recommendation: Replace 'grew at a similar rate to peers' reported H1 2026 pre-tax profit' with the actual spread, e.g. 'grew 9%, in line with Standard Chartered's 9% pre-tax profit growth and below Barclays' 17%'.

claim_findings.passage: Basel 3.1 is expected to drive a modest reduction in RWAs on 1 January 2027 (management gave the figure in the call as a range measured in billions of pounds).
claim_findings.evidence: The claim's own quote states the figure: 'Basel 3.1 will drive a reduction of around six to eight billion on the 1st of January '27.' The claim_text withholds it and substitutes the evaluative word 'modest', which the speaker never used -- against a group RWA base this is management's own stated range, not a characterisation the transcript supports. The parenthetical reads as a workaround for numeric grounding rather than a description, and it leaves the downstream reader of Section 4 ('an anticipated Basel 3.1 RWA reduction at the start of 2027 [claim-043]') with no magnitude at all.
claim_findings.recommendation: State the range in words in claim_text, mirroring the quote (e.g. 'a reduction of around six to eight billion pounds'), and drop 'modest'.

claim_findings.evidence: Period-labelling consistency (Python cannot judge this): claim-014 ('Group deposits up £5 billion (1%) in Q2 2026'), claim-011 ('up over £5 billion or 1% versus Q1') and claim-015 ('grew around £25 billion in Q2 2026') all describe an incremental quarterly flow but are labelled 'as of 30 Jun 2026', a point-in-time stamp. The directly comparable claim-013 ('Commercial lending balances up £3.1 billion in Q2 2026'), sourced from the same seg-0003 passage and the same kind of flow, is labelled '3 months to 30 Jun 2026'. Each of the three mixes a stock level and a quarterly flow in one claim, and the label fits only the stock half.
claim_findings.recommendation: Label the flow component '3 months to 30 Jun 2026' consistently with claim-013, or split each into a stock claim ('as of 30 Jun 2026') and a flow claim ('3 months to 30 Jun 2026').

My number's around ten and a half billion'). Same pattern verified for claim-052.

outlook_findings.passage: A second upside path is faster-than-guided delivery on the further £2 billion of 2027-2030 gross cost saves [claim-037], which management said it would "out-deliver" and return to shareholders if capacity allowed, rather than reinvest into higher costs [claim-034]
outlook_findings.evidence: The quoted commitment is real -- Charlie Nunn says it in seg-0012: 'If we can out-deliver, we will out-deliver, and then we'll go back to the framework that William always lays out around if we have additional capital, we'll look at the alternatives ... distributing to our shareholders is an important way that we think we add value.' But it is nowhere in claims.json: no claim covers seg-0012. The id the brief attaches to it, claim-034, is the 2030 RoTE/capital-generation target ('We're targeting a RoTE of circa 20% and more than 225 basis points of capital generation in 2030') and says nothing about out-delivering cost saves or about returning versus reinvesting. Python's citation check passes because the id resolves; the inference does not trace to it. The same unanchored quotation is repeated in Section 8: 'Progress of the £2 billion 2027-2030 gross cost-save programme against the "out-deliver, then return to shareholders" framing [claim-034][claim-037]'.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Add a claim quoting seg-0012 (Charlie Nunn, 'If we can out-deliver, we will out-deliver...') and cite that claim in Sections 6 and 8 in place of claim-034, or delete the quoted commitment and rest the second upside path on claim-037 alone.

outlook_findings.passage: Management explicitly declined to quantify AI's revenue and cost contribution to the 2027-2030 targets beyond a narrowly defined in-year 2026 benefit figure disclosed only qualitatively on this call, deferring a fuller AI framework to the January 2027 year-end results (see Section 9) — this is a genuine gap in an otherwise fully quantified guidance set, not an oversight on our part.
outlook_findings.evidence: Two problems. First, this is a material assertion about what management said, made in Section 3 and repeated at the head of Section 9 ('Management declined to give a full 2030 AI revenue/cost quantification, citing uncertainty over customer adoption and regulatory approval...'), with no claim citation at either place -- no claim in claims.json covers seg-0014 or seg-0036, the two segments that actually contain it. Second, 'disclosed only qualitatively' is wrong: in seg-0036 Nunn gives the figure, 'we would stay focused for now on delivering the 100 million in year benefit for a narrow definition of AI', and separately quantifies the earlier November framing at '70% of the revenue was linked to digital and AI, and 60% of our gross cost saves'. The benefit was narrowly scoped, not unquantified. The deferral itself is accurate ('We'll have a discussion next year at the year-end results in January').
outlook_findings.recommendation: Add claims for the seg-0036 deferral and the £100 million in-year AI benefit, cite them in Sections 3, 8 and 9, and change 'disclosed only qualitatively on this call' to state the £100 million narrow-definition figure that was in fact given.

outlook_findings.passage: The observable indicator would be the quarterly hedge yield print (last given as trending toward the 3.7% refinancing rate [claim-047]) failing to compress even as market rates hold
outlook_findings.evidence: claim-047 establishes only that the plan assumes a 3.7% hedge refinancing rate and that the market is at least 50bps above it. 3.7% is a forward-looking reinvestment assumption for the 2027-2030 plan (seg-0005: 'Our expectations for the reinvestment on our hedge are predicated upon this assumption and average around 3.7% over the period'), not an observed print. Nothing in claims.json or in the transcript reports a 'quarterly hedge yield print ... last given as trending toward 3.7%'. The upside case's stated confirming indicator is therefore built on a disclosure this run does not contain, and it also inverts the logic -- a realised yield converging on 3.7% would confirm the plan assumption, not the upside. The same claim id is stretched again in Section 8, where it is cited for 'hedge notional growth versus the "pretty modest" guidance'; that phrase comes from seg-0011 but is not in claim-047's text or quote.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Drop the parenthetical 'last given as trending toward the 3.7% refinancing rate', or replace it with what claim-047 does support (realised reinvestment yields printing above the 3.7% plan assumption). Add a claim for the 'pretty modest notional growth' statement in seg-0011 if Section 8 is to keep monitoring it.

outlook_findings.passage: net interest margin rose to 322bps in Q2 from 319bps for H1
outlook_findings.evidence: Period-comparison error of the kind Python cannot catch: both numbers are grounded in claim-017, but 319bps is the H1 average, which already contains Q2's 322bps -- it is not an earlier period the margin rose from. The real sequential move is +5bps in the quarter (claim-017: 'a second quarter margin of 322 basis points up five basis points in the quarter'), implying a Q1 figure around 317bps. As written the sentence presents a within-period average as a prior-period baseline.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Rewrite as 'net interest margin was 319bps for H1, with the Q2 margin at 322bps, up 5bps quarter on quarter [claim-017]'.

outlook_findings.passage: cost:income ratio of 50.4% for H1 and 49% in Q2, already inside the below 50 percent full-year guidance band [claim-005][claim-022]

outlook_findings.recommendation: Attach the guidance-band clause to the Q2 figure only, e.g. 'cost:income ratio of 50.4% for H1, with Q2 at 49%, already inside the below-50% full-year guidance band'.

summary: No high or critical findings, so the run may proceed with warnings. Round 1's blocking finding is genuinely fixed: the 2030 structural-hedge guidance of more than £9 billion is now claim-056, it appears in the Section 3 guidance set, the Section 6 upside case is anchored on it plus the analyst's mark-to-market estimate (claim-057) and Chalmers' response (claim-058), and Section 9's 'cannot be quantified' statement has been narrowed to the RoTE-versus-consensus gap where it is now true. claim-055 no longer implies a Lloyds consensus beat and now names each metric explicitly, the RWA-optimisation overclaim in Sections 2 and 5 is gone, and the equity-base rebuttal (claim-059) and the £200 million remediation assumption (claim-060) are both surfaced as counter-evidence. Three medium findings remain, and they share one root cause: material management statements that are accurate against the transcript but have no claim anchoring them, so the brief either leaves them uncited or attaches an unrelated claim id that Python's citation check passes because the id merely resolves. The Section 6 and 8 'out-deliver, then return to shareholders' quotation is Charlie Nunn's from seg-0012 but is cited to claim-034, the 2030 RoTE target, which says nothing of the kind. The AI-quantification deferral is asserted twice with no citation at all, and it mischaracterises the disclosure -- management did give a figure, the £100 million narrow-definition in-year benefit in seg-0036, whereas the brief says it was disclosed only qualitatively. The Section 6 monitoring indicator invents a 'quarterly hedge yield print last given as trending toward the 3.7% refinancing rate' that no claim or transcript line contains; 3.7% is a forward plan assumption, not an observed print. Six lower findings follow, including an uncited NIM path in the downside case, Section 2 still describing management's RoTE answer as pure appeal-to-conservatism while claim-059 contradicts it, a within-period NIM baseline presented as a prior period, and inconsistent quarterly-flow period labels across claims 011, 014 and 015. Source correctness, temporal integrity and process compliance are clean: both peer sources are genuine and pre-event, the post-event NatWest and HSBC files are archived but unused, validation.json and outlook-validation.json are both ok == true, the injection scan is empty, and neither the signal card nor the brief shows cross-sector template drift.
